question: Could sending root X, changing the clock or relying on warm-b replace the intermediate and wrong-name checks?

criteria.instruction: No. L is issued by I and I by R; X does not issue I and is not a configured trust root. A transmitted root is not automatically trusted. Reference-time validity already holds and moving the clock does not supply I. warm-b's cache masks the missing presentation. Even L/I must reject the other service name, as the negative control shows.
Use certificate issuer relationships, T9 trust/name/time rules and the clean versus warm/wrong-name checks.
Reject unapproved trust changes, time overrides and ignored name mismatches. Do not claim a warm-client success establishes correct clean-client deployment.
